rationale: Correct RCO's legal form, ownership roster and active concession footprint. Current filings establish Red de Carreteras de Occidente, S.A.P.I. de C.V. as the legal company, Abertis at 53.12%, GIC at approximately 29.04% within the BBVA trust block and the AFORE/HSBC block at 17.84%. Preserve ICA and Goldman Sachs Infrastructure Partners as former owners, distinguish trustee substitutions from economic transfers, and do not treat Mundys or Atlantia as direct RCO shareholders.

beforeImage.name: Red de Carreteras de Occidente, S.A.B. de C.V.
beforeImage.description: Red de Carreteras de Occidente operates concessioned toll roads and related mobility services in western and central Mexico. Its customers are passenger and freight users moving through one of the country's main industrial and logistics corridors. The operating model is asset-heavy and concession based, with cash flow generated from toll collection and associated road services over long asset lives. Recent company materials describe more than 1,100 kilometers of managed highways, while transaction materials at the time of the Abertis and GIC acquisition described the asset as one of Mexico's largest motorway operators. RCO was constituted in 2007, and Abertis and GIC completed the acquisition of 72.3% of the company in 2020, with GIC disclosed at 21% of the equity.
beforeImage.headquarters: Jalisco, Michoacán, Guanajuato, Aguascalientes, and Zacatecas

afterImage.description: Red de Carreteras de Occidente, S.A.P.I. de C.V. operates the Red Vía Corta toll-road platform in western and central Mexico. Its current portfolio comprises the FARAC I, COTESA and AUTOVIM concessions across Jalisco, Michoacán, Guanajuato, Aguascalientes and Nayarit; CONIPSA and COVIQSA expired in 2025 and 2026. The filed active centerline network is approximately 844.3 kilometers after those expiries. Current economic ownership is Abertis at 53.12%, GIC at approximately 29.04% within the BBVA México trust block and multiple Mexican AFORES at 17.84% through the HSBC México trust block. ICA and Goldman Sachs Infrastructure Partners are former owners. Trustee substitutions and Mundys' indirect interest through Abertis are not separate economic ownership changes, and no later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.
